Fig. 9: Quantitative comparison of the three navigation conditions: without assistance, with robot guide dog, and with our Co-Ego system. From left to right, the plots show (a) number of collisions, (b) task completion time, and (c) perceived safety. Error bars denote participant variability.

Fig. 10: NASA-TLX cognitive load measured while completing tasks under three conditions: without assistance, with the robot guide dog, and with our Co-Ego system. Lower scores indicate lower cognitive load.
Fig. 5: Flowchart of the dual-perception priority-based navigation algorithm.

Fig. 3: Viewpoint asymmetry between human and robot egocentric views. (a) RGB and (b) point cloud from the user’s neck-worn camera capture the hanging lamp at head height but miss the ground-level cabinet. (c) RGB and (d) cost map from the quadruped’s point cloud detect ground-level obstacles (red regions) with a navigable path in between (blue regions) but remain blind to the overhead lamp.
Fig. 8: Illustration of the three navigation conditions evaluated in our study.
